title: Economic gate: parallel warm-chains by default, rate window, static prefix
description:
In skills/ticks/references/agent-runner.md: the "Dispatch modes and the economic gate" section (mode list and heuristics paragraph), loop step 4a, and the "Never silently degrade" discipline rule.

The text must say:
- Parallel warm-chains are the default: K chains in K worktrees, grouped by subsystem and tier, file-disjoint.
- Chains are balanced so the longest chain is about the longest single tick; a tick that is itself the longest runs solo.
- Target: 2-3 implementers per epic unless the work is large. Any other choice is a noted one, in the dispatch ledger.
- The cold start is paid per implementer, not per tick; ticks stay small for resume granularity.
- The rate window (a subscription's usage window) caps dispatch width as a gate input, not a surprise.
- An identical static prefix across implementers launched together, in this order: system prompt, repo instruction file, learnings head, rules; per-tick data after it. Mark the cache-accounting benefit "unverified".
- The template's base check carries a per-tick commit, so a byte-identical prefix is not claimed; document the ordering only.

Shared vocabulary (verbatim across all three parallel chains, which do not see each other):
- Files: `.tick/learnings.md` is the always-read head (at most 4096 bytes: hard rules plus an index of the body's categories). `.tick/learnings-ref.md` is the looked-up body (Problem/Cause/Rule entries, at most 16384 bytes, at most 800 bytes per entry). The 800-byte entry limit applies to the body only. The engine owns the format; the project owns the content.
- Check labels in implementer reports: the tick-gate command verbatim, `by-path run`, `planted fault`.
- Check outcomes: `ran clean`, `went red and changed the code`, `went red, not from this change`, `not applicable`.
- Terms: "parallel warm-chains", "warm turn", "retire" (an implementer is retired after the final review).
- Existing section titles in agent-runner.md stay as they are. The gate names are "tick gate" and "wave gate", already defined.
Spec (source of truth): docs/thoughts/2026-11-12-lean-epics.md. Edit only skills/ticks/ (never an installed copy) unless your task names other files. Keep the engine's terse voice; criteria, not step lists.
acceptance_criteria:
- `grep -n 'rate window' skills/ticks/references/agent-runner.md` and `grep -ni 'unverified' skills/ticks/references/agent-runner.md` both hit inside "Dispatch modes and the economic gate"
- "2-3 implementers" is present; no remaining sentence makes parallel-wave (one fresh implementer per tick) the default for wide waves
- "Never silently degrade" stays consistent with the new default
